articles.title: Napoli provide update on Scott McTominay after undergoing heart surgery in Manchester
articles.summary: Napoli have confirmed ex-Manchester United star Scott McTominay's heart surgery 'was a complete success,' with the 29-year-old set to rest for two weeks befo...
articles.body:
Napoli have confirmed that Scott McTominay has undergone a successful surgical procedure to address a minor cardiac condition. The former Manchester United midfielder was recently found to have a mild benign arrhythmia, an irregular heart rhythm that was not considered to be serious but did require medical intervention.

The 29-year-old went under the knife in Manchester on Tuesday, with Napoli declaring the operation a 'complete success.' The Serie A club added that their midfielder is anticipated to return to the field following the upcoming international break.

"On Tuesday morning, Scott McTominay underwent an ablation procedure at Spire Manchester Hospital," Napoli said in a statement, via The Mirror . "The operation was a complete success. McTominay will rest for two weeks and then resume training."

The Scotland international has also played down the seriousness of the issue, saying at a recent awards ceremony: "I'm fine, the procedure was something I'd planned to do with the club for quite a while."

McTominay's absence due to the procedure caused him to sit out Napoli's 3-2 road loss to Inter Milan last Saturday. He will remain sidelined for three additional Napoli fixtures, among them their UEFA Champions League home opener against Arsenal on Wednesday.

Max Allegri will be hoping to have McTominay back in contention when his side welcomes Frosinone on October 10 in their first fixture following the international break. Napoli have dropped points in two of their opening three Serie A matches, leaving them sitting 12th in the standings, six points adrift of league leaders AS Roma.

Scotland will also be forced to do without McTominay as new manager Sebastien Pocognoli begins his tenure. Coming off a disappointing World Cup group stage exit, Scotland will aim to regroup across four Nations League fixtures scheduled between September 26 and October 6.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

McTominay's long-term prospects in Naples have also generated considerable discussion this week. Despite being contracted until 2028, there remains uncertainty over whether he will put pen to paper on a new deal.

He joined Napoli under Antonio Conte two years ago in a transfer worth £25.7 million (around $33.7 million), claiming the Italian title in his debut season and earning the Serie A Player of the Season award. Napoli sporting director Giovanni Manna addressed the questions surrounding the 29-year-old in an interview with DAZN .

"Scott said he doesn't know if he'll renew at this time," Manna explained. "He has a two-year contract, we want to do it, and he wants to do it, too. It's not always easy to make things coincide, but we're trying."

McTominay departed United in the summer of 2024 after spending over two decades with the Red Devils, having made 255 first-team appearances and lifting both the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

articles.summary: Muy buenas tardes a todos. Arrancamos con la narración en directo del partido Borussia Dortmund - Villarreal, correspondiente a la primera jornada de
articles.body:
Muy buenas tardes a todos. Arrancamos con la narración en directo del partido Borussia Dortmund - Villarreal , correspondiente a la primera jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League . El estreno en la máxima competición continental para ambos equipos, que quieren empezar con buen pie.

El conjunto alemán ha comenzado la temporada de forma impecable. Ha ganado tres partidos oficiales de los cuatro que ha disputado , dos de la Bundesliga y uno de la DFB Pokal. Perdió la Supercopa de Alemania ante el Bayern de Múnich. La intención del equipo de Niko Kovac es extender esta buena racha a la Champions.

Para este partido, el técnico del conjunto alemán tiene varias bajas importantes. No estarán Schlotterbeck, Mané, Konstantelias y Emre Cam , por lesión, ni tampoco Bensebaine , por sanción.

El Villarreal afronta este partido con dudas por el titubeante inicio de temporada , en el que ha sumado dos puntos de 12 posibles . Por este motivo, el partido de hoy se presenta como una oportunidad inmejorable para revertir la situación y dar un impulso definitivo al submarino.

Iñigo Pérez , técnico del conjunto amarillo, tiene las bajas de Foyth y Carlos Romero , que no podrán ser de la partida por lesión. Estas bajas obligarán al técnico a realizar cambios, aunque no serán los únicos. Todo hace indicar que también habrá cambio en la portería . Luiz Junior lleva varios partidos a un bajo nivel, por lo que Iñigo podría apostar hoy por colocar a Gulasci bajo palos.

El partido arranca a las 21.00 horas en el BVD Stadion. Se espera, como siempre, un lleno absoluto, con más de 81 mil aficionados en las gradas y un ambiente espectacular. El encuentro lo dirigirá el colegiado italiano Simone Sozza , mientras que el responsable del VAR será su compatriota Daniele Chiffi . Queda presentado el partido. Desde ya os vamos a ir contando todas las novedades que se vayan produciendo en torno a este partidazo de Champions. COMENZAMOOOOOOOOOOOOSSSSSSSS.

articles.title: SEC schedules meeting to decide whether to 'terminate' LSU as conference member
articles.summary: On Tuesday morning, the league filed an amended complaint in its lawsuit against LSU, head coach Lane Kiffin and school officials.
articles.body:
The SEC has called a Thursday meeting to "decide whether to terminate Louisiana State University ('LSU') as an SEC member institution," according to an amended complaint the conference filed Tuesday morning in its lawsuit against LSU .

In its filing, the SEC accuses LSU of a "lack of institutional control" that the league requires, highlighting what it believes to be ineffective administrative authority over Kiffin.

The first-year Tigers head coach, long ensnared in drama — including last year's soap opera that surrounded him departing Ole Miss for the LSU job on the brink of a College Football Playoff appearance — has flirted with bringing aboard a pair of players who spent time on NFL rosters as rookies this offseason . That's a transaction the SEC has forbid in the wake of several athletes from the high school class of 2022 trying to capitalize on the NCAA's new five-for-five eligibility model , which wasn't intended to grandfather in those who exhausted their eligibility amid the 2025-26 academic year.

While LSU didn't roster former Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright and former New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Zxavian Harris for a Week 1 beatdown of Clemson, Kiffin has left spots open for their potential additions midseason.

Both Wright and Harris, who played for Kiffin at Ole Miss last season before going undrafted, were granted a preliminary injunction for a fifth year of eligibility last week in a Baton Rouge court . As part of that decision, though, LSU — along with the NCAA and SEC — was prohibited from taking action to prevent the players from competing .

Kiffin said Saturday on ESPN's "College GameDay" that the choice to omit Wright and Harris from the Tigers' Week 1 roster was in "the best interest of the team and the university," citing the "big picture" of LSU as well as the uncertainty regarding the possible consequences the program and school could face.

But the SEC's Tuesday filing alludes to how Kiffin remarked on ABC at the end of an on-field halftime interview during LSU's 51-10 season-opening victory later that day, "It took everything to not say, 'Imagine if we had pro players.'"

At the time, the 11th-ranked Tigers were up 31-3 at home.

articles.title: College Football Coaches Poll 2026 Week 2 Rankings Released with Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: There wasn't much movement in the Week 2 American Football Coaches Association Coaches Poll released Tuesday after the vast majority of top-25 teams were victorious in Week 1.
articles.body:
There wasn't much movement in the Week 2 American Football Coaches Association Coaches Poll released Tuesday after the vast majority of top-25 teams were victorious in Week 1.

Ohio State continues to lead the way following its 56-3 decimation of Ball State. Here is a full rundown of where the rankings stand with the Buckeyes on top (first-place votes in parenthesis) :

Report Card Grades for CFB's Top QBs 🧑‍🏫

The majority of the top 10 teams that were in action in Week 1 won easily against a lower level of competition, including the Buckeyes, who saw their Heisman Trophy candidates in quarterback Julian Sayin and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith get the season off to an ideal start.

Sayin threw for 320 yards and three touchdowns, while Smith finished with eight receptions for 151 yards and two scores in OSU's easy victory.

Things did not come so easily for No. 6 Oregon, though, as the Ducks were pushed to the limit at home by Boise State.

The Ducks trailed for most of the first half, but they came to life in the second half, and Heisman Trophy-contending quarterback Dante Moore was at his best when the team needed him most.

With less than eight minutes remaining in the game, Moore broke a 27-27 score by hitting wide receiver Dakorien Moore for what proved to be a game-winning, 62-yard touchdown.

Despite the win, Oregon dropped four spots from No. 2 to No. 6, making the Ducks one of the biggest fallers in the poll.

Most highly ranked teams played cupcakes from lower-end conferences, but No. 4 Notre Dame and No. 7 Miami tested themselves to some degree against power-conference teams and passed them with flying colors, as the Fighting Irish beat Wisconsin 41-13 and the Hurricanes decimated Stanford 45-6.

Perhaps the most impressive performance of the week belonged to No. 8 LSU, who were the biggest risers, going from 13th to eighth.

In their first game under head coach Lane Kiffin, the Tigers destroyed then-No. 23 Clemson by a 51-10 score.

LSU ran wild on Clemson with 309 yards on the ground, including 113 yards and two touchdowns by both quarterback Sam Leavitt and running back Dilin Jones.

Given their poor showing, it comes as little surprise that Clemson dropped out of the top 25, making way for Florida after the Gators crushed Florida Atlantic 66-21, as well as Virginia, as the Cavaliers beat NC State 34-8 in Week 0.

Aside from LSU, SMU was the biggest riser among teams that were in the top 25 last week, going from 20th to 17th thanks to Monday night's 27-24 road win over Florida State.

Although it remained ranked, Michigan was a massive faller, as it went from 16th to 24th despite a victory. The eight-spot drop was the most among all teams in the poll.

It appeared as though the Wolverines had lost at home to Western Michigan when their last-ditch Hail Mary attempt hit the ground, but one second was controversially put back on the clock, and head coach Kyle Whittingham's team took advantage.

Quarterback Bryce Underwood's second Hail Mary was perfect, and wide receiver JJ Buchanan came down with it for a 47-yard touchdown to give Michigan a less-than-convincing 13-12 triumph.

Michigan will be part of one of the two games pitting ranked opponents against each other next week when it faces No. 10 Oklahoma, while No. 1 Ohio State will clash with No. 3 Texas.

articles.title: Lionel Messi and World Cup winner Lamine Yamal on 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or nominee list
articles.summary: It’s that time of year again when the soccer world turns its attention to the Ballon d’Or awards — accolades given to the man and woman deemed to be the best player in the world.
articles.body: It’s that time of year again when the soccer world turns its attention to the Ballon d’Or awards — accolades given to the man and woman deemed to be the best player in the world. The nominees for both categories were released on Tuesday, starting what will be an Oscar-worthy campaign ahead of the awards ceremony in London on October 26. Given the top 30 men’s and women’s players were listed, there is little space for controversy at this point. On the men’s side, England striker Harry Kane, French attacker Kylian Mbappé and Spanish youngster Lamine Yamal are the three leading contenders. Kane scored 73 goals for Bayern Munich last season, although failed to win the Champions League or World Cup — two trophies which often determine where this award goes. The same is true of the ever-impressive Mbappé, but the Real Madrid superstar has arguably the most talent of anyone on the list. Then, of course, there’s Yamal – a 19-year-old phenom who has won almost everything you can in the sport as a teenager. He helped Spain win the World Cup this summer, although he wasn’t at his electric best. Eight-time winner of this award Lionel Messi has also been included in the longlist, mainly due to his brilliant performances in the World Cup. He is very unlikely to win, though. Full list of the 30 men’s nominees Ballon d’Or Feminin For the women, it’s a little clearer. Barcelona’s Alexia Putellas is surely the standout after her string of performances for the Catalan club, helping it win the quadruple last season before her move to the London City Lionesses this summer. Her teammate Ewa Pajor is another contender to consider, one of eight players from Barcelona to be nominated. Three-time defending winner Aitana Bonmatí of Barcelona missed a large part of the season with a broken leg suffered in late November 2025, so missed out on the list this year. Full list of the 30 women’s nominees Who votes? A team of world-leading soccer journalists votes on who they think is the best player in the world. The award is often controversial given the subjective nature of the process, and yet has felt increasingly important to players in recent years.

articles.title: Club Brugge 2-3 Aston Villa: Unai Emery's side end scoring concerns as Nicolas Jackson nets first goal in Champions League win
articles.summary: Report as Aston Villa earn thrilling victory over Club Brugge in Champions League league phase; John McGinn, Emiliano Buendia and Nicolas Jackson score in superb first-half display; Villa hadn't netted in three Premier League games; Unai Emery's side had 21 shots with nine on target
articles.body:
The Europa League winners had failed to score in their first three Premier League matches, having had just one shot on target, but their attack clicked in Belgium as John McGinn, Emiliano Buendia and Nicolas Jackson struck to kickstart their season.

Villa had 14 efforts in a scintillating first-half performance that began with McGinn expertly side-footing a trademark first-time shot into the bottom left corner after being set up by Pau Torres' driving run out of defence.

Club Brugge's expansive approach contributed to a breathless tie and the hosts equalised when Hugo Vetlesen swept a low shot into the corner, although Buendia restored Villa's lead within three minutes, tapping in from close range following good work by Joao Gomes.

Villa threatened constantly on the counter-attack and their third goal came when Jackson ran in behind to try and latch onto Torres' long ball forward, beating goalkeeper Yann Sommer to the ball and slotting into an empty net for his first goal since joining in a club-record £65m move.

The hosts pulled one back just after the hour mark through Nicolo Tresoldi's penalty, awarded for handball on Aaron Wan-Bissaka after the referee was sent to the pitchside monitor, but despite coming under heavy pressure, Villa held on for victory.

11: GOAL! McGinn scores Villa's first goal of the season with a lovely side-footed finish.

19: EQUALISER! Vetlesen produces his inner McGinn by slotting the ball into the bottom right corner.

22: VILLA LEAD AGAIN! The hosts are level for just three minutes as Buendia arrives to tap-in from close range after good work from Gomes.

43: JACKSON SCORES! The striker caps Villa's superb attacking performance by beating Sommer to the ball and slotting into an open net.

61: GOAL! Game on as Tresoldi slots away a penalty after Wan-Bissaka's handball.

69: WOODWORK! Emery makes three subs before Villa are about to defend a corner and then Tresoldi's glancing header at the set piece is pushed onto the post by Suzuki.

82: OFF THE LINE! Bogarde is denied from wrapping up the win for Villa as his shot is cleared.

Villa's counter-attacking blueprint can spark their season

This time last year Aston Villa had started slowly but a win in Europe breathed life into their season - the same can happen after this morale-boosting display.

Villa discovered their scoring touch following a worrying first three league matches and the way in which they picked apart Club Brugge has given Unai Emery a blueprint to follow.

His side had just 35 per cent possession in Belgium yet produced 21 shots in total with nine on target as their frontline tore the hosts apart on the counter repeatedly.

Nicolas Jackson thrives on running in behind, which is how he scored his goal, while Emi Buendia's craft and John McGinn's ability to protect the ball and pick passes on the counter were mixed perfectly with George Hemmings' dribbling ability on the other flank.

The challenge now is whether Emery is willing to take that idea into the Premier League. Villa will not have the same space or freedom against every opponent, but if they can reproduce the intensity, pace and ruthlessness shown in Bruges, this could prove to be the performance that kick-starts their season.

Emery: Another step forward with complete performance

"The hard work is even when we are not winning. I am so happy today and thankful because we know how we are in the way with the responsibility we and I have.

"The players have a responsibility too, the older players need to guide to keep our standard high, to show everybody that this is the only way to achieve our targets. We are improving after Brighton and after Hull City.

"Today was another step forward. We must work hard - it is the only way. This is the process that we must try to set. Today we did one very important step forward, being resilient when we were struggling.

"The subs impacted the game well and we regained control of the game. Brugge are strong and confident here. We did a very complete match, competing in 90 minutes."

McGinn: New Villa passed test with huge win

Aston Villa captain John McGinn on win over Club Brugge:

"It was so important to show a real gritty performance and get a victory at a very tough place to play. The [home] supporters were excellent [and Brugge are a] very impressive club, so to win tonight was huge for us.

"It's a new Villa and it was a big test for the new players to dig in. It was Joao Gomes and George Hemmings' first Champions League games. It's not easy to go away at a place like this in difficult weather conditions.

"Club Brugge were pushing and pushing and pushing and we had to stand strong. We managed to do that."

On his goal: "Pau Torres made a great run through the middle and I just tried to use the defender to elevate the goalkeeper's sight line, so I just passed it in the corner.

"As I've got older, I've tried to use that finish a lot more and just place it in the corner rather than smashing it. In the second half, I had a big chance to do the same."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: El Betis deja su carta de presentación con una remontada de Champions
articles.standfirst: Se sobrepone dos veces a una desventaja ante el Lille y termina ganando; Mbappé, expulsado
articles.summary: Se sobrepone dos veces a una desventaja ante el Lille y termina ganando; Mbappé, expulsado
articles.body: El Betis ha dejado su carta de presentación en su ansiado regreso a la Champions. Más de 20 años habían pasado desde la última vez que los verdiblancos escucharon la música de la máxima competición continental. Pero en su visita al Lille en Francia demostraron que este equipo comandado por Pellegrini y capitaneado por Isco nada tiene que ver con el que en su día vivió su primera experiencia entre los más grandes del fútbol europeo. Hasta dos veces lograron los verdiblancos sobreponerse a un marcador adverso hasta terminar sumando sus tres primeros puntos de esta fase de liga. Bartra, con dos sensacionales remates de cabeza, rescató a su equipo las dos ocasiones en que los de Davide Ancelotti lograron ponerse por delante en el marcador. Y Troy Parrott, demostrando que es un nueve con potencia y muchísimo gol, completó la vuelta al marcador para regocijo de los más de 800 aficionados béticos que acompañaron a su equipo en el Estadio Pierre-Mauroy, actual Decathlon Arena. El Betis regresó al torneo estrella de la UEFA con la intención de mirar a los ojos al Lille, pero pronto descubrió que cualquier desajuste se paga caro en la máxima competición continental. Los verdiblancos comenzaron con personalidad, tratando de combinar por dentro con Isco y de cargar el área rival. Roro dejó el primer aviso a los dos minutos, con un disparo que se marchó por encima del larguero. Pero los franceses no tardaron en encontrar el punto débil de la zaga verdiblanca, el costado derecho de su ataque, por el que no tardaron en hacer daño... El equipo de Davide Ancelotti, peligroso en las transiciones y en los centros laterales, castigó a los de Pellegrini en el minuto 12. Tiago Santos encontró en profundidad a Ethan Mbappé, que recortó a Facundo y puso un centro con rosca de zurda al segundo palo. Allí apareció Ueda, completamente solo, para cabecear a la red. El gol hizo perder claridad al Betis, que pasó de una puesta en escena prometedora a perder de golpe la clarividencia que había mostrado de inicio. Poco a poco, el equipo verdiblanco trató de recuperar metros, aunque le costaba encontrar precisión en los últimos metros. Antony acumuló varias decisiones desacertadas en las inmediaciones del área, hasta que en el minuto 33, tras una corrección del Ingeniero desde la banda, acertó con la elección. El brasileño recortó hacia dentro y filtró un pase a Bellerín que terminó provocando un córner. En la segunda jugada desde la esquina, Fornals puso un sensacional balón al área y Bartra, llegando desde atrás, lo cabeceó a la red para devolver la igualdad al marcador. La alegría del empate, sin embargo, duró apenas tres minutos. Junior llegó muy tarde a un balón dividido y estuvo cerca de cometer penalti en una acción que terminó en córner. No le hizo falta una jugada de pizarra demasiado elaborada a los franceses para marcar. Balón al área y Alexsandro, aprovechando la errática defensa en zona de los andaluces, se elevó por encima de todos y conectó un cabezazo a la escuadra, imposible para Valles. El 2-1 castigaba de nuevo a un Betis que había demostrado capacidad para reaccionar, pero que seguía concediendo demasiado en su área. Pese al golpe, los verdiblancos tuvieron una oportunidad inmejorable para volver a empatar antes del descanso. En el minuto 40, una contra espectacular terminó con Isco llegando por la izquierda y sirviendo un balón a Parrott para que lo empujara a la red. El delantero, sin embargo, se llenó de balón y remató por encima del larguero. Una ocasión clarísima que recordó a la que ya había desperdiciado ante el Levante con 2-2 en el marcador, en un encuentro que el Betis terminó perdiendo por 5-2. El irlandés, autor del gol de la victoria frente al Real Madrid el pasado viernes, volvió a ponerse de gol, algo que hace con una facilidad pasmosa, pero perdonó en la definición. El Betis regresó del descanso decidido a cambiar el rumbo del partido y apenas necesitó cuatro minutos para encontrar el empate. Parrott peleó un balón en la banda hasta provocar una falta y, en el 49', Isco puso el balón en el área para que Bartra volviera a aparecer como un delantero. El central catalán remató a la red y firmó su doblete, devolviendo la igualdad a un encuentro en el que los verdiblancos habían hecho méritos para no marcharse por detrás al vestuario. El 2-2 dio todavía más impulso al equipo de Pellegrini. Apenas un minuto después, Natan recuperó bien el balón en campo contrario y encontró a Antony en la frontal. El brasileño se acomodó la pelota para su pierna derecha y soltó un disparo que se marchó fuera por poco. El Betis había vuelto al césped con una marcha más y el Lille, pese a haber tenido un día más de descanso que su rival, empezaba a sufrir ante la velocidad y la determinación de los verdiblancos. La remontada se completó en el 53' en una acción que tuvo a Riquelme y Parrott como protagonistas. El extremo inició una gran conducción por el centro, resistió un agarrón y continuó avanzando hasta encontrar al delantero irlandés. Parrott encaró a Ngoy, se marchó por potencia y sacó un zurdazo cruzado al palo más alejado que terminó en la red. El 2-3 suponía el premio a la ambición del Betis y, además, la redención del atacante, que antes del descanso había desperdiciado una ocasión clarísima para empatar. El partido dio otro vuelco apenas dos minutos después. Natan tocó en el hombro a Ethan Mbappé y el futbolista francés respondió con un codazo en la cara del brasileño. El árbitro acudió al monitor del VAR para revisar la acción y, tras comprobar las imágenes, mostró amarilla al central verdiblanco y roja directa al jugador del Lille. No ha sido la semana de los Mbappé contra el Betis... Los franceses se quedaban con 10 cuando acababan de perder una ventaja de dos goles, mientras que los andaluces pasaban a disponer de superioridad numérica para afrontar el resto del encuentro. Pese a la expulsión, el Lille no se rindió. El equipo francés trató de apretar y siguió buscando el costado derecho de su ataque, la zona por la que más problemas había generado al Betis desde el inicio. Pellegrini respondió moviendo el banquillo para proteger la ventaja y evitar cualquier contratiempo disciplinario. Retiró al amonestado Natan para dar entrada a Valentín y dio descanso a Isco con la incorporación de Fidalgo. Pocos minutos después, sustituyó también a Facundo, que había visto una tarjeta amarilla, para introducir a Marc Roca. Con 2-3 en el marcador, a los de Ancelotti no les quedaba otra que mirar al área rival. Pero cada vez que adelantaban líneas el Betis encontraba espacios para correr. Antony, con un mal pase, desperdició una contra clarísima para buscar el cuarto. El partido parecía decidido, pero salió Giroud y le dio a los franceses el impulso que necesitaban para creer que el empate era posible. Provocó dos lanzamientos de esquina seguidos y tuvo el 3-3 en sus botas en una gran ocasión desbaratada por Valentín Gómez. Pero tras el susto, los de Pellegrini entendieron que tenían que defenderse con balón, con posesiones largas. Así consiguieron desactivar la efervescencia que había provocado Giroud y gozaron de alguna buena ocasión para sentenciar. Sobre todo un zurdazo de Antony que sacó Özer a córner y una contra final de Parrott. No hubo que sufrir más en el alargue para disparar el optimismo en Heliópolis. El regreso a la Champions más de dos décadas después no pudo ser mejor para un Betis que suma sus primeros tres puntos y buscará en casa ante Oporto y Feyenoord en las dos próximas jornadas intentar poner un pie en las rondas eliminatorias por primera vez en su historia.
